worldFact.locationContext: Danakil Depression · Afar Region, Northeast Africa
worldFact.fact: Situated 130 metres below sea level in the Danakil Depression, Dallol holds the record for Earth's highest average year-round temperature at 35°C (95°F). Its acidic geothermal springs erupt boiling neon-green brine, toxic sulfur fumes and magnesium salts where almost no microbial life can survive.
